UGA003.reason: Matooke cooked with cow intestines. No generic photo shows this and an offal-and-banana substitute would mislead.

UGA009.reason: Ghee whipped with rock salt to a pale creamy ceremonial sauce. A photo of any white sauce would misrepresent it, and eshabwe is not in stock libraries.

UGA023.reason: Bitter garden eggs with ground dried silverfish. Two ingredients stock libraries do not carry, in a combination nothing else resembles.

UGA030.reason: Sweet banana and groundnut steamed in a banana-leaf parcel. The parcel is the dish; an unwrapped substitute shows nothing.

UGA051.reason: Fresh shelled beans and pasta with katunkuma bitter berries. The berries are the point and they are not photographed.

UGA055.reason: Street-fried cow lung in instant noodle broth. Nothing in a stock library is this, and a noodle-soup photo would hide the one ingredient that defines it.

UGA061.reason: Roasted grasshoppers. Stock libraries carry live grasshoppers, not cleaned and roasted nsenene — a live-insect photo would be actively wrong.

UGA062.reason: Winged termites, dewinged and roasted or pounded to flour. Same problem as nsenene: the available insect photography is of live insects.

UGA063.reason: Roasted crickets. As above — a live cricket is not the dish.

UGA070.reason: Sun-dried cowpea leaf ground to a powder. A pantry item, not a plated dish, and not photographed.

UGA072.reason: Small sun-dried Lake Victoria fish in groundnut paste. Nkejje are specific and are not in stock libraries.

UGA081.reason: Spider plant and amaranth leaves in groundnut sauce finished with sour milk. Jobyo is not photographed and the sour milk is invisible in any substitute.

UGA082.reason: Skinned beans with dried silverfish. A bean-stew photo hides the mukene, which is half the dish.

UGA084.reason: Ground unroasted sesame, pressed and rolled into balls. The single most distinctive northern Ugandan dish and entirely unphotographed.

UGA086.reason: Millet beer drunk from a shared pot through long straws. The shared pot is the dish; no stock photo has it.

UGA087.reason: Lugbara sorghum beer. Not photographed, and a beer glass would misrepresent it entirely.

UGA089.reason: Fermented sorghum and honey brew from Kigezi. Not photographed.

UGA090.reason: Sorghum drink served in wooden cups. Not photographed.

UGA091.reason: Mingled millet and cassava bread — a dark brown mound. Ugali photos are white and would be the wrong colour and the wrong grain.

UGA093.reason: Mashed pigeon peas with shea butter, used to anoint Lango clan leaders. Ceremonial and unphotographed.

UGA094.reason: Termites ground to a paste. See the other insect entries.

UGA097.reason: A brown cooking liquid made from sieved plant ash. Not a plated dish and not photographed.

UGA098.reason: Salt made by burning dried salty leaves. Not photographed.

UGA099.reason: Pounded wingless termites cooked in leaves. See the other insect entries.

UGA100.reason: Juice squeezed from pounded young maize. Not photographed, and a glass of milk would be wrong.

UGA101.reason: Ground maize tied in a leaf and boiled into a block. The leaf parcel is the dish.

UGA103.reason: Boned fish mashed into groundnut paste. One of very few documented Madi dishes and not photographed.

UGA110.reason: Fermented termites rolled into balls and hardened in salted water. See the other insect entries.

UGA112.reason: Stiff sorghum porridge from Karamoja. Same colour-and-grain problem as karo.

UGA118.reason: Cassava-flour staple, mingled stiff. A white ugali photo is the wrong grain.
